newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares rise, Bombay index up 1.66 pct.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares rise, Bombay index up 1.66 pct.

text.p: ** Stocks close higher for fourth straight
session, market rally gains strength
** Foreign funds, local players bid aggressively
** All-round optimism lures small investors--traders
** Bombay 30-share index jumps 55.93 points, or 1.66 pct,
to close at 3,418.32, off 3,443.56 day's high
** Delhi index rises 1.60 percent, Calcutta index up 0.51
pct and Madras index adds 1.97 pts
** National bourse index rallies 23.75 pts to 980.35
Strong buying support from foreign funds and local players helped blue chip stocks close higher on Friday taking the market's winning run to four straight days this week, dealers said.
"There is a growing feeling among fund managers not to get left behind in the rally," said institutional dealer Govind Agarwal at local brokerage Motilal Oswal.
Bombay stocks have surged five percent this week on market hopes about government policies to revive capital markets.
The policy package is expected to boost industrial growth and revive sagging capital markets.

Sharp movements in small cap stocks was a pointer to improved liquidity and a lot of demand being generated in the market. "Retail investors are also showing interest...follow-up support is being seen," Agarwal said.

Buying was focussed on pharmaceutical and consumer non-durable stocks, dealers said. Foreign funds were keen buyers in Bajaj Auto, Hind Lever, MTNL, Colgate, Tata Tea, Castrol, Glaxo and Procter & Gamble.
"Revival of buying by foreign funds has brought a sharp change in the market's behaviour," said Vinod Aggarwal at Mass Financial Services.
Widespread market expectations of tax breaks and positive government announcements will be the key factors pushing up stock prices next week, analysts said.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's top 30-share index has rallied 154.26 points, or 4.7 percent, to end at 3,418.32 this week -- up nearly 11 percent since the close of 1996.

Bajaj Auto rose 39.0 rupees to 980.0, Colgate 9.25 to 255.50, Hindalco 23.75 to 745.0, ITC 16.0 to 346.0, MTNL 11.0 to 249.0, Tata Tea 8.50 to 229.75 and L&T 8.0 to 245.0. SBI lost 1.25 rupees to 253.75 and TISCO 3.50 to 185.50.
-- ANSHUMAN DAGA, Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
